question.problem: Using the cross product curvature formula, find the curvature of $r(t)=⟨t,\,\sqrt{t}⟩$ as a function of $t.$
question.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{4t}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{4t+1}{4t}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{4t+1}}{2\sqrt{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-\frac{1}{4\sqrt{{t}^{3}}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(t)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t) & =⟨1,\,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,-\frac{1}{4\sqrt{{t}^{3}}},\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{4\sqrt{{t}^{3}}} & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} &  \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{4\sqrt{{t}^{3}}}\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-\frac{1}{4\sqrt{{t}^{3}}}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the cross product is

$$
‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖=\frac{1}{4\sqrt{{t}^{3}}}.
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{4\sqrt{{t}^{3}}})}{{(\frac{\sqrt{4t+1}}{2\sqrt{t}})}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{4\sqrt{{t}^{3}}})}{(\frac{\sqrt{(4t+1)^{3}}}{8\sqrt{{t}^{3}}})} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{(4t+1)^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
